Sankey Diagram

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/sankey-diagram.Rmd
sankey-diagram.Rmd

Basic Sankey Diagram 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_sankey(
    orientation = "h",
    node = go_sankey_node(
      label = c("A1", "A2", "B1", "B2", "C1", "C2"),
      color = c("blue", "blue", "blue", "blue", "blue", "blue"),
      pad = 15,
      thickness = 20,
      line = go_sankey_node_line(
        color = "black",
        width = 0.5
      )
    ),
    link = go_sankey_link(
      source = c(0, 1, 0, 2, 3, 3),
      target = c(2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5),
      value = c(8, 4, 2, 8, 4, 2)
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Basic Sankey Diagram",
    font = go_font(size = 10)
  )

Create Canvas 

library(plotly.core)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_sankey(
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)),
    orientation = "h",
    valueformat = ".0f",
    valuesuffix = "TWh"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Energy forecast for 2050, UK - Department of Energy & Climate Change",
    font = go_font(size = 10),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE)
  )

Add Nodes 

library(plotly.core)
library(jsonlite)

json_file <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.js/master/test/image/mocks/sankey_energy.json"
json_data <- fromJSON(json_file, simplifyVector = FALSE)
sankey <- json_data$data[[1]]

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_sankey(
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)),
    orientation = "h",
    valueformat = ".0f",
    valuesuffix = "TWh",
    node = go_sankey_node(
      label = unlist(sankey$node$label),
      color = unlist(sankey$node$color),
      pad = 15,
      thickness = 15,
      line = go_sankey_node_line(
        color = "black",
        width = 0.5
      )
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Energy forecast for 2050, UK - Department of Energy & Climate Change",
    font = go_font(size = 10),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE)
  )

Style Sankey Diagram 

library(plotly.core)
library(jsonlite)

json_file <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/plotly.js/master/test/image/mocks/sankey_energy_dark.json"
json_data <- fromJSON(json_file, simplifyVector = FALSE)
sankey <- json_data$data[[1]]

go_figure() |>
  add_sankey(
    domain = go_domain(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)),
    orientation = "h",
    valueformat = ".0f",
    valuesuffix = "TWh",
    node = go_sankey_node(
      label = unlist(sankey$node$label),
      color = unlist(sankey$node$color),
      pad = 15,
      thickness = 15,
      line = go_sankey_node_line(
        color = "black",
        width = 0.5
      )
    ),
    link = go_sankey_link(
      source = unlist(sankey$link$source),
      target = unlist(sankey$link$target),
      value = unlist(sankey$link$value),
      label = unlist(sankey$link$label)
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Energy forecast for 2050<br>Source: Department of Energy & Climate Change, Tom Counsell via <a href='https://bost.ocks.org/mike/sankey/'>Mike Bostock</a>",
    font = go_font(size = 10, color = "white"),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, showticklabels = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE, showticklabels = FALSE),
    plot_bgcolor = "black",
    paper_bgcolor = "black"
  )

Define Node Position

The following example sets the x and y of go_sankey_node() to place nodes in the specified locations, except in the snap arrangement (default behaviour when node.x and node.y are not defined) to avoid overlapping of the nodes, therefore, an automatic snapping of elements will be set to define the padding between nodes via the node’s pad. The other possible arrangements are: 1) perpendicular 2) freeform 3) fixed

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_sankey(
    arrangement = "snap",
    node = go_sankey_node(
      label = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"),
      x = c(0.2, 0.1, 0.5, 0.7, 0.3, 0.5),
      y = c(0.7, 0.5, 0.2, 0.4, 0.2, 0.3),
      pad = 10 # 10 Pixel
    ),
    link = go_sankey_link(
      source = c(0, 0, 1, 2, 5, 4, 3, 5),
      target = c(5, 3, 4, 3, 0, 2, 2, 3),
      value = c(1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2)
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(title = "Sankey with manually positioned node")

Reference

See go_sankey() for more information and options!
